mariam: Heads-up — running into an issue using the Redwood JS SDK inside a Next.js Edge middleware on Vercel. Need help narrowing whether this is a bundler vs edge runtime problem.

oliver: Can you paste the error + a minimal repro?

mariam: Production error is `TypeError: fetch is not a function` when the middleware calls the client. Local `next dev` works fine. We're on Next 13.5 and using `export const runtime = 'edge'` in the middleware.

jess: That smells like a vendored/node-only fetch polyfill getting bundled. Edge has native `fetch` — if the SDK bundled `node-fetch` or `undici` as CJS, that could overwrite/mis-wire things in the bundle.

mariam: I grepped the SDK build in node_modules and found a `require('node-fetch')` in `dist/index.cjs` for v0.14.2 — looks like the node path got bundled into the edge build.

rui: Yeah that explains it. CJS `require` + edge ESM runtime -> runtime can't resolve `fetch`. Approach: prefer the global `fetch` when available, otherwise dynamically import `undici`/`node-fetch` in node-only builds. Example pattern:

```js
// pseudo
const _fetch = typeof fetch !== 'undefined' ? fetch : (await import('undici')).fetch;
```

But note: top-level `await import` needs async init or lazy getter.

oliver: Also watch the TypeScript side — our SDK types extend `RequestInit` and pull `body`/`headers` shapes that differ between Node and Edge lib types. Teams without DOM lib get TS errors in edge projects.

jess: Workaround is `skipLibCheck` but that's nasty. Longer term: provide distinct type entrypoints (`./edge.d.ts` and `./node.d.ts`) or export a thin runtime-agnostic type for the public API.

mariam: I'll prototype a small patch to stop bundling `node-fetch` into the browser/edge build and add runtime detection. Will also add a short migration note in the README.

rui: Also flag the auth retry logic — we use `setTimeout` in our retry helper. In strict edge/worker environments timers and global scope can differ (Workers have `setTimeout` but other edge runtimes may not). Use `globalThis.setTimeout` or better, avoid timers and use non-blocking backoff with `AbortController` where possible.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: Canary on vercel-prod failed during the staged rollout. Observed 429 spike after the revert.

jess: Proposed plan: 1) remove node-only polyfills from edge bundle, 2) add `exports` pkg fields for `./edge` and `./node` entrypoints, 3) tighten types to not assume DOM libs, 4) add a CI smoke test that builds and runs a minimal Next Edge middleware sample against a preview Vercel environment.

mariam: I'll open the PR and attach a minimal Next repro (middleware + small serverless route) that reproduces the fetch/type issue. Assigning to @oliver and @jess for review.

oliver: Thanks — one extra note: Next's bundler sometimes pulls `main` (CJS) fields if `exports` aren't present. Make sure SDK's package.json has `type: "module"` for the ESM bundle and `exports` that point edge-friendly files.

mariam: :thumbsup: will include CI steps and run the sample on vercel preview before merging.
